short: Binding SnO2 Nanocrystals in Nitrogen-Doped Graphene Sheets
title: Binding SnO2 Nanocrystals in Nitrogen-Doped Graphene Sheets as Anode Materials for Lithium-Ion Batteries

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: SnO2 anodes offer high Li capacity but lose it through volume change and particle aggregation on cycling. Binding SnO2 nanocrystals inside N-doped graphene sheets should give a high-capacity, long-life, high-rate anode.

states.title: Structure state
states.head: The nanocrystals are rutile SnO2, unchanged by the N-RGO. SnO2 crystallites are about 4-6 nm.

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: SnO2NC@N-RGO delivers ~1100 mAh g-1 reversible capacity from the second cycle. Graphene encapsulation and binding buffer SnO2 volume change and stop nanocrystal aggregation, keeping electrical contact.
states.detail: Absorbed: p1 (PRP/value), m1 (MEC/pathway), m2 (MEC/pathway). Premises: Solid-state diffusion time scales as L^2/D, so smaller crystals lithiate faster

states.title: Performance state
states.head: The anode keeps ~1350 mAh g-1 after 500 cycles at ~99% Coulombic efficiency. The anode retains ~420 mAh g-1 at 20 A g-1 and recovers ~1000 mAh g-1 back at 0.5 A g-1

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Binding SnO2 nanocrystals in N-doped graphene yields a high-capacity, long-life, high-rate Li-ion anode

nodes.title: TEM:HRTEM, F1
nodes.head: HRTEM shows densely packed lattice-fringed crystallites about 4-6 nm across
nodes.note: sized against the 5 nm bar; SnO2 (110) fringes labelled; wavy N-RGO layers at the edge
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for s2 (o3).

nodes.title: SEM, F1
nodes.head: High-magnification SEM shows smooth wrinkled sheet surfaces with no exposed particles
nodes.solves: SnO2 nanocrystals are encapsulated beneath a carbon (graphene) skin
nodes.note: 4-6 nm crystallites would be near the SEM resolution limit, so absence is weak evidence
nodes.necessity_reason: No member reaches image_support shown, and s4 keeps shown support from o5.

nodes.title: XRD, F2
nodes.head: Composite and bare SnO2NC XRD patterns coincide and match the standard SnO2 lines; no extra phase
nodes.solves: The nanocrystals are rutile SnO2, unchanged by the N-RGO
nodes.note: reflections broad (nanocrystalline); no graphite (002) peak near 26 deg separate from SnO2 (110)
nodes.necessity_reason: s1 keeps shown support from o2 after removal.

nodes.title: XAS:XANES, F2
nodes.head: C K-edge XANES of the composite nearly overlays N-RGO, with slightly higher pi* and sigma* intensity
nodes.solves: SnO2 nanocrystals are chemically bound to the N-RGO sheets
nodes.note: no new peak appears; differences are small and could reflect normalisation, so binding is only weakly shown
nodes.necessity_reason: No member reaches image_support shown and s6 has no other figure-backed support.

nodes.title: TEM:SAED, F1
nodes.head: SAED rings index to SnO2 (110), (101), (200), (211), (301)
nodes.solves: The nanocrystals are rutile SnO2, unchanged by the N-RGO
nodes.necessity_reason: s1 keeps shown support from o1 after removal.

nodes.title: EDS:AES, F2
nodes.head: AES depth profile: Sn rises from ~5 at% at the surface to ~21 at% after 0.2 min sputtering, then ~24 at%
nodes.solves: SnO2 nanocrystals are encapsulated beneath a carbon (graphene) skin
nodes.note: F2c surface AES survey dominated by C with weak Sn and O
nodes.detail: o5: AES depth profile: Sn rises from ~5 at% at the surface to ~21 at% after 0.2 min sputtering, then ~24 at%
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for s4 (o5).

nodes.title: MICRO, F4
nodes.head: After cycling the active material is a compact ~2-3 um agglomerate
nodes.solves: Graphene encapsulation and binding buffer SnO2 volume change and stop nanocrystal aggregation, keeping electrical contact
nodes.note: F4f (300 nm bar) shows a dense ~2.5 um particle; F4a (100 nm bar) shows only a boxed field of packed nanocrystals, so a pre-cycling particle outline is not available for comparison; the cycled electrode also contains binder and additive
nodes.necessity_reason: No member reaches image_support shown, and m1 keeps shown support from o4, o13.

nodes.title: ATOM:DFT, ECHEM:CV, EDS:spectrum, PHYS:surfacearea, XPS:region, F2, F3, F4
nodes.head: EDS maps: C, O and Sn signals co-extensive and even across the mapped area. XPS survey shows a weak N 1s peak near 400 eV beside Sn, O and C.
nodes.op: assign features, read characteristic point, register colocated views
nodes.note: dark patches coincide in all three channels (thickness), not Sn-free regions; region boxed in F4a inset N 1s fitted with two components near 401 and 399.5 eV; N content not quantified in the figure DFT-derived distribution; isotherm rises almost linearly to ~230 cm3 g-1 with no clear hysteresis loop
nodes.detail: o4: EDS maps: C, O and Sn signals co-extensive and even across the mapped area; o7: XPS survey shows a weak N 1s peak near 400 eV beside Sn, O and C; o9: Pore-size distribution (inset) peaks near 2-3 nm; o11: CV: a cathodic peak at ~0.95 V appears only in cycle 1; peaks at ~0.15 V (cathodic) and ~0.5 and ~1.25 V (anodic) persist
nodes.necessity_reason: m1, m2, p1 keeps shown support from o13, o10 after removal.

nodes.title: evidence, F3
nodes.head: First discharge ~1850 mAh g-1, first and later charges ~1050-1150 mAh g-1
nodes.solves: SnO2NC@N-RGO delivers ~1100 mAh g-1 reversible capacity from the second cycle
nodes.note: first-cycle Coulombic efficiency ~60%; 2nd and 3rd curves nearly overlap
nodes.detail: o10: First discharge ~1850 mAh g-1, first and later charges ~1050-1150 mAh g-1
nodes.necessity_reason: p1 keeps shown support from o11 after removal.

nodes.title: EDS:spectrum, F3, F4
nodes.head: The late capacity rise ends ~20% above the early reversible capacity, which buffering alone does not predict. After 500 cycles, C, O and Sn maps still overlap across the particle, but Sn shows bright Sn-rich streaks
nodes.solves: Graphene encapsulation and binding buffer SnO2 volume change and stop nanocrystal aggregation, keeping electrical contact
nodes.op: compare across conditions, cross check consistency
nodes.note: rise from ~1000 to ~1350 mAh g-1 between cycles 20 and 500; contributions from electrolyte-derived films or carbon activation are not separated EDX I_O:I_Sn rises from 0.87 (F4b) to 1.31 (F4g) and C dominates the cycled spectrum (SEI, binder, conductive additive)
nodes.detail: o13: The late capacity rise ends ~20% above the early reversible capacity, which buffering alone does not predict; o15: After 500 cycles, C, O and Sn maps still overlap across the particle, but Sn shows bright Sn-rich streaks
